9| // batchKey fingerprints one accepted batch for duplicate detection.
10| // The key covers tenant, producer, and the content digest, but
11| // deliberately NOT the receive timestamp: a producer that retries the
12| // same batch after a network error must collide with its earlier
13| // self, and timestamps would make every retry unique.
14| func batchKey(tenant, producer string, payload []byte) string {
15| 	h := sha256.New()
16| 	h.Write([]byte(tenant))
17| 	h.Write([]byte{0})
18| 	h.Write([]byte(producer))
19| 	h.Write([]byte{0})
20| 	var n [8]byte
21| 	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(n[:], uint64(len(payload)))
22| 	h.Write(n[:])
23| 	h.Write(payload)
24| 	return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)[:16])
25| }
26| 
27| // shardFor buckets a key into one of the dedupe shards. Sharding is
28| // stable across restarts so a key seen before a crash lands in the
29| // same shard's window after recovery, and a fleet of edges spreads
30| // keys identically for the same shard count.
31| func shardFor(key string, shards int) int {
32| 	var v uint32
33| 	for i := 0; i < 4 && i < len(key); i++ {
34| 		v = v<<8 | uint32(key[i])
35| 	}
36| 	return int(v % uint32(shards))
37| }
